## Executive Summary

- **#1 (HIGH, tool, ~5h)**: Kilo #12546 honors per-server MCP timeout across
  all clients. The per-server timeout field in cline_mcp_settings.json was
  only read by the VSCode extension's tools/call path; metadata requests
  (tools/list, resources/*, prompts/*) and SDK client requests timed out at
  hardcoded 5s/1.5s constants, causing slow servers to fail despite a
  configured timeout. Now resolves timeout once per client (60s default, 1s-
  3600s bounds, clamps milliseconds/seconds mix-ups), applies it to
  initialize, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, prompts/list; runs
  metadata fetches in parallel (four sequential requests blocked for four
  timeout bounds when a server hangs after initialize); keeps failed servers
  visible with disconnected entry carrying the error; rejects tool calls on
  connections without a client with controlled error. Alexi uses `@model
  contextprotocol/client@^2.0.0` (package.json line 34-35). Applicable if
  Alexi has MCP server integration with configurable timeouts or if timeout
  handling can be improved. Size: HIGH (~5h: add per-server timeout parsing,
  apply to all request types, parallel metadata fetch, failed server
  visibility, reject tool calls on failed connections, test timeout
  lifecycle).

## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Honor per-server MCP timeout across all clients (tool, ~5h, HIGH)

- **What**: Kilo #12546 honors per-server MCP timeout across all clients.
  The per-server timeout field in cline_mcp_settings.json was only read by
  the VSCode extension's tools/call path. Everywhere else used hardcoded
  constants: the SDK client timed out all requests at 5s and initialize at
  1.5s, and the extension's metadata requests (tools/list, resources/*,
  prompts/*) timed out at 5s. Slow servers failed despite a configured
  timeout (#7635, #12344). Now resolves timeout once per client (60s default,
  1s-3600s bounds, clamps out-of-range values so a milliseconds/seconds mix-
  up cannot become hours) and applies it to every request: initialize, tools/
  list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/templates/list, prompts/list.
  Unconfigured servers keep the fast 1.5s initialize probe so startup is no
  slower than before; a configured timeout raises that budget for slow-
  starting servers. Four post-connect metadata requests now run in parallel
  (previously sequential, so a server that hangs after initialize blocked
  connectToServer for four timeout bounds). Failed servers now register a
  disconnected entry carrying the error so the server stays visible in the
  list instead of silently disappearing. Tool calls on connections without a
  client reject with a controlled error naming the server and its last
  connection error, instead of dereferencing the null client and throwing a
  TypeError. Timeout errors now name the bound and the field to increase.
- **Why**: Alexi uses `@modelcontextprotocol/client@^2.0.0` and
  `@modelcontextprotocol/server@^2.0.0` (package.json line 34-35). Applicable
  if Alexi has MCP server integration with configurable timeouts or if
  timeout handling can be improved. The pattern is generic: per-resource
  timeout configuration that is only honored on one code path while other
  code paths use hardcoded constants, causing slow resources to fail despite
  explicit configuration. Size: HIGH (~5h: add per-server timeout parsing to
  MCP config loader, apply resolved timeout to all request types not just
  tools/call, parallelize metadata fetches, register failed servers with
  disconnected entry carrying error, reject tool calls on connections without
  a client with controlled error, add timeout lifecycle tests).
- **Source**: Kilo PR #12546 "fix(mcp): honor per-server timeout (seconds)
  across all clients" (merged 2026-07-30T06:12:34Z, commit `8f3a9c7`). Full
  PR body at https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/12546. Fixes #7635,
  #12344.
- **Category**: tool. **Size**: HIGH (~5h: add per-server timeout parsing,
  apply to all request types, parallel metadata fetch, failed server
  visibility, reject tool calls on failed connections, test timeout
  lifecycle). **Status**: HIGH signal (per-server timeout config not honored
  is a reliability/UX issue; Alexi uses MCP v2; applicable if Alexi has MCP
  server integration with timeout configuration).

#### 2. Add bash tree-sitter tags for repomap support (tool, ~3h, MODERATE)

- **What**: Aider #5132 adds bash tree-sitter tags for repomap support. Bash
  shell scripts were not parsed by tree-sitter, so function definitions and
  significant structures were missing from the repomap. Adds tree-sitter-bash
  grammar with tags query capturing function definitions (function_definition
  node, name field), variable assignments (variable_assignment node, name
  field), loops (for_statement, while_statement, until_statement nodes),
  conditionals (if_statement, case_statement nodes), and comments (comment
  node). The repomap now includes bash function names, significant control
  structures, and variable declarations, improving code navigation for shell
  scripts.
- **Why**: Alexi has tree-sitter support via existing tools. The definitions
  tool (`src/tool/tools/definitions.ts`) uses tree-sitter for code symbol
  extraction. Applicable if Alexi has bash/shell script analysis needs or if
  repomap coverage for shell scripts is desired. The pattern is generic:
  extending tree-sitter grammar coverage to a language that was previously
  unsupported, improving code structure extraction and navigation. Size:
  MODERATE (~3h: add tree-sitter-bash grammar dependency, write tags query
  for bash function definitions and significant structures, integrate with
  existing tree-sitter tool infrastructure in definitions tool, test on shell
  scripts in Alexi repo like .github/workflows agent retry-with-backoff
  blocks).
- **Source**: Aider PR #5132 "feat: add bash tree-sitter tags for repomap
  support" (merged 2026-07-30T04:21:18Z, commit `7b9e8f4`). Full PR body at
  https://github.com/aider-ai/aider/pull/5132.
- **Category**: tool. **Size**: MODERATE (~3h: add tree-sitter-bash grammar,
  write tags query, integrate with existing tree-sitter tool infrastructure,
  test on shell scripts). **Status**: MODERATE signal (bash tree-sitter tags
  improve repomap coverage for shell scripts; Alexi has tree-sitter support
  via definitions tool; applicable if bash/shell script analysis is desired).

#### 3. Expand ANTHROPIC_MODELS list with recent Claude model names (provider, ~1h, MODERATE)

- **What**: Aider #5173 expands ANTHROPIC_MODELS list with recent Claude

  `sanity_check_models` to map a bare Claude model name (no provider prefix)

  20260205`, `claude-opus-4-7-20260416`. All added names have corresponding
  entries in `aider/resources/model-settings.yml`.
- **Why**: Alexi supports Anthropic models via SAP AI Core (`src/providers/
  sapOrchestration.ts`, `src/providers/index.ts`). Applicable if Alexi has a
  similar model-name-to-provider mapping that could be stale or if new Claude

  name list that must be kept in sync with upstream model releases, or models

  model name mappings in src/providers/ and routing-config.json, add missing
  recent Claude models if applicable, verify model catalog entries exist for
  new models, test model resolution).
- **Source**: Aider PR #5173 "Expand ANTHROPIC_MODELS list with recent Claude
  model names" (merged 2026-07-30T03:45:29Z, commit `4c8e1a2`). Full PR body
  at https://github.com/aider-ai/aider/pull/5173.
- **Category**: provider. **Size**: MODERATE (~1h: audit model name mappings,
  add missing recent Claude models, verify model catalog entries exist).
  **Status**: MODERATE signal (stale model name list is a model resolution
